name: SEER: Self-Guided Function Calling in Large Language Models via Stepwise Experience Recall
venue: EMNLP 2025 Findings (Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025, pages 10846-10849; DBLP key conf/emnlp/CuiHXZWZWX25). Preprint arXiv:2508.15214 (submitted 21 Aug 2025).

maintained_repo_url: N/A (the GitHub repo is the static official implementation, last commit Sep 28 2025; no continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list).
task_domain: tool-use / function calling (multi-step and multi-turn). Specifically tool-augmented LLM agents performing multi-step function calling for tool-augmented QA (ToolQA, 8 real-world domains) and multi-turn real-world agentic tasks (tau-bench airline & retail). Falls under tool-use and decision-making.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, training-free (no parameter updates) experience-replay setting. An LLM-based agent must achieve a user-defined goal g by interacting with a user and a set of external tools over a finite horizon of T steps, building an interaction history H_t = {o_0, a_0, ..., o_t} where observations come from both user input/feedback and tool outputs and actions are natural-language responses or tool invocations. SEER is a self-guided in-context-learning method: it retrieves prior successful trajectories from a continually-updated experience pool to guide the next decision, and accumulates new successful trajectories online during deployment. Supervision: no fine-tuning; for tasks without explicit success signals it uses an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator to decide whether a finished trajectory should be retained. Settings span one-turn multi-step QA (ToolQA) and dynamic multi-turn user-agent interaction (tau-bench, with a GPT-4o user simulator).
what_is_retrieved: experiences / trajectories: past SUCCESSFUL multi-step tool-use trajectories stored in an online experience pool, retrieved as in-context fewshot exemplars to guide the LLM's next action. Each retrievable item is a complete trajectory together with a structured experience representation (trajectory embedding, first-query embedding, inferred user intent, and tool-invocation path).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes itself. The experience pool is incrementally and online-augmented with the agent's own past successful trajectories during deployment (seeded with a small initial demonstration pool: 8 examples for ToolQA, 2 for tau-bench). It is not a static external corpus and not a manually curated library; it is a self-generated, continually-expanding experience store. Maximum pool size capped at 1000.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: SEER retrieves a fixed number k of highest-scoring trajectories (default k=4) ranked by a weighted multi-dimensional relevance score. No minimal-set-completeness objective and no precision-driven variable-size recommendation; k is a tuned hyperparameter (ablated over k in {0,2,4,6,8}, best at k=4).
retrieval_unit: full trajectory: a complete successful multi-step tool-use trajectory tau = {o_0, a_0, o_1, a_1, ...} retrieved as a fewshot exemplar. The trajectory is described by a structured experience tuple d^tau = <E^tau, E^q, I^tau, U^tau> = (trajectory embedding, first-query/first-observation embedding, inferred discrete user intent, and the directed tool-invocation path u_1 -> u_2 -> ... -> u_n). So retrieval is at the granularity of a whole task trajectory, scored using both trajectory-level and tool-chain-level signals.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The retrievable store is built incrementally during deployment from the agent's self-collected successful trajectories (continual experience accumulation), seeded by a small initial demonstration pool. Not an offline-frozen index: the pool expands online as new tasks are completed (capped at 1000 entries). Contrasts explicitly with prior static, pre-collected/offline datasets.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index augmented with metadata/context keys. Each entry stores a dense trajectory embedding (and a separate first-query embedding) plus structured metadata: an inferred discrete user-intent label and the tool-invocation set/path U. Scoring combines flat cosine similarity over embeddings with metadata-keyed signals (tool-set overlap, intent equality). No explicit dependency/knowledge graph or hierarchical category->tool topology; the tool-chain is represented as a directed path within each entry but the pool itself is a flat metadata-keyed store.
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) retriever combined with rule/metadata scoring. Trajectory and query embeddings produced by the off-the-shelf bge-large-en-v1.5 embedding model; cosine similarity (s1) is combined with a lexical/set-overlap tool-chain coverage score (s2) and an indicator intent-match score (s3) into a single weighted relevance score. Effectively a hybrid of dense similarity + symbolic metadata matching; not BM25, not learned/generative.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): the retriever uses a frozen pretrained bge-large-en-v1.5 embedder and a hand-designed weighted scoring function Score = sum_i lambda_i s_i with fixed equal weights lambda_1=lambda_2=lambda_3=1/3. There is no contrastive training, LM-feedback, downstream-task or preference (Bradley-Terry) optimization, no RL/value-based learning of the retriever. The retrieval components (similarity, toolchain coverage, intent match) are selection heuristics; only the experience pool content changes online (via the LLM-judge retain decision), not the retriever parameters. The Limitations section notes the fixed weighting could be made task-aware/learned in future work.
query_construction: The query is the current interaction history H_t. SEER extracts from H_t the same structured representation used for stored items: a trajectory embedding E^{H_t} (the running interaction history), the first-query/observation embedding E^q, the inferred user intent I^{H_t} (classified by the LLM itself from the initial query against a predefined discrete intent set), and the observed tool-invocation set U^{H_t}. These are matched against each candidate experience tuple. Intent is inferred via an LLM-based intent recognizer (Appendix A.1) rather than manual annotation. A query-based ablation variant instead keys only on the first-query embedding E^q.
query_granularity: step/state-level (stepwise). Retrieval is performed from the CURRENT interaction history H_t at the agent's decision points (hence 'Stepwise Experience Recall'), conditioning on the evolving history rather than only the initial query. (Note: on ToolQA, a one-turn multi-step benchmark, the user query does not change across turns, so trajectory-level and query-only representations are less divergent; the stepwise advantage is more pronounced on tau-bench multi-turn tasks.)
when_to_retrieve: iterative / stepwise: SEER performs experience recall to guide the LLM's next decision based on the current interaction history, recalling top-k examples (D_recall) at decision steps rather than only once at t=0. It is a fixed (schedule-based) stepwise recall, not uncertainty-triggered or a learned router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: stepwise recall is triggered unconditionally at decision steps, computing the multi-dimensional relevance score over the experience pool and inserting the top-k trajectories. There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned-complexity-classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated trigger; retrieval is invoked on the standard schedule of the agent loop.
reranking: None (single-stage). Candidate trajectories are scored once by the weighted multi-dimensional relevance score (trajectory similarity + toolchain coverage + intent match), sorted in descending order, and the top-k are taken directly. No second-stage cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond ranking/truncation: the top-k retrieved successful trajectories are injected as fewshot exemplars without compression, decomposition, distillation, or distractor filtering. (A SEER+Reflection variant adds Reflexion-style error identification/correction at inference to mitigate cumbersome/suboptimal examples that caused overthinking on simple tasks, e.g. Coffee-Easy, but this is reflection on the agent's own reasoning, not refinement of the retrieved context itself.)
tool_document_engineering: N/A. SEER does not retrieve or engineer tool/skill DESCRIPTIONS; the retrievable items are past task trajectories, not tool docstrings. Tools are provided by the benchmarks (ToolQA tool set spanning SQL/DB, Python, math, text retrieval, graph; tau-bench airline 13 tools / retail 15 tools).
index_content_separation: N/A. No separation of a lightweight retrievable index from heavy on-demand content; the structured experience tuple (embeddings + intent + tool path) is used both to score and to fetch the full trajectory, which is loaded wholesale as a fewshot exemplar.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a tool index (SEER's growing store holds trajectories, not tools). However the EXPERIENCE pool itself is dynamic/live-synchronized: it is updated online via an insert operation after each successfully-judged task (Algorithm 2). Tool integration is via standard function-calling / tool wrappers (SQL, Python, Math, Text, Graph, Table) in ToolQA and the tau-bench tool APIs; no RapidAPI/MCP/RESTful tool-store sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial / implicit via toolchain coverage. SEER represents each trajectory's tool usage as a directed invocation path U = u_1 -> u_2 -> ... -> u_n and scores candidates by toolchain coverage s2 = |U^{H_t} intersect U^{tau'}| / |U^{H_t}|, rewarding overlap in tools used. The ablation shows s2 is most important on HARD questions, where the model must navigate intricate dependencies among multiple tools. However coverage is a set-overlap proportion, not an explicit inter-tool dependency graph, shared-auth model, or dependency-aware reranker; ordering/dependency edges are stored in the path but not separately scored.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the top-k retrieved successful trajectories (D_recall) are inserted as in-context fewshot demonstrations into the LLM prompt to guide the agent's next decision (tool selection, parameter generation, tool-chain planning). No fine-tuning, no latent-token injection; pure in-context learning over a frozen LLM (Qwen2.5-7B / Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct).
planning_integration: per-step interleaved / retrieve-then-act stepwise. SEER weaves recall into the agent's decision loop: at decision points it recalls top-k trajectories from the experience pool conditioned on the current interaction history and uses them as exemplars to guide the next action; the agent then acts, observes, and continues. No MCTS/tree search and no explicit hierarchical subtask decomposition; planning is the LLM's in-context multi-step tool-use guided by recalled exemplars. On one-turn ToolQA this is effectively task-conditioned exemplar guidance; on multi-turn tau-bench it interleaves with evolving user intent.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call / per-decision-step within a rollout (stepwise). Recall is woven into the multi-step tool-use loop at the agent's decision points (the 'stepwise' core), as opposed to a single per-answer retrieval. On the one-turn ToolQA setting the practical interleaving is coarser because the query is fixed across turns; the stepwise/per-step character is most meaningful in tau-bench's multi-turn interactions.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar reuse: retrieved successful trajectories are injected as-is as fewshot demonstrations; the LLM implicitly adapts them to the current task during generation. No explicit case-rewriting, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning at solve time. The optional SEER+Reflection variant adds execution-feedback-style self-correction (Reflexion) to the agent's reasoning, a light adaptation layer, but retrieved cases themselves are not edited.
retrieved_item_representation: raw trajectory: the surface form injected into the prompt is the raw successful interaction trajectory (sequence of observations and actions / tool calls) used as a fewshot exemplar. The structured tuple (embeddings, intent label, tool path) is used internally for scoring, not injected as the demonstration content.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: raw trajectory (single concrete demonstration). SEER recalls concrete past successful trajectories rather than distilled strategies, state-aware guidelines, reusable workflows, or procedural skills; abstraction is left to the LLM's in-context generalization. (This contrasts with ExpeL, which additionally distills cross-task natural-language insights.)
noise_robustness_mechanism: Multi-dimensional relevance scoring + LLM-judge gating on writes. (1) Quality of retrieved context is controlled by retaining only SUCCESSFUL trajectories (LLM-as-a-judge verifies task completion before a trajectory enters the pool), so noisy/failed experiences are filtered out at write time; (2) the three-component score (trajectory similarity, toolchain coverage, intent match) reduces retrieval of irrelevant exemplars; (3) a moderate k (best at 4) avoids overwhelming the model with excessive/distracting demonstrations (performance declines for k>4); (4) the optional SEER+Reflection identifies and corrects errors induced by suboptimal/cumbersome exemplars. No retriever-aware adversarial training or explicit distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: episodic: an experience pool of past successful task trajectories (a continually-growing trajectory replay memory). Not a distilled skill-library, workflow store, knowledge graph, or latent memory.
write_back: Yes. After completing a task, SEER forms an experience tuple (tau, d^tau) and inserts the trajectory into the experience pool D <- D union {(tau,d)} if the trajectory is judged successful (continual experience accumulation, Algorithm 2). This is the central self-guided self-improvement mechanism.
online_growth: Yes. The experience pool grows online during deployment/test-time: successful trajectories are incrementally added so the pool 'continuously expands' and model performance improves over time. Explicitly contrasted with prior methods that rely on static, offline, pre-collected datasets. Pool size is capped at 1000 entries.
write_back_trigger: on-success only, judged reflectively by an LLM evaluator. After a task finishes, an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator compares the agent's output to a reference answer and returns a binary success/failure judgment; only trajectories judged successful are written to the pool. The evaluator is designed to tolerate minor discrepancies (formatting variations, slight numerical differences) and still count them as success. No failures are written; writes are gated by the success judgment rather than a fixed every-task schedule.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only. Only successful trajectories are stored and retrieved; failed/negative trajectories are discarded (not retained, not used as contrastive or corrective examples). The LLM evaluator's role is to keep failures OUT of the pool. (The optional Reflection add-on uses within-episode error signals to self-correct, but failed trajectories are not persisted as negative memory.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (with a capacity cap). Successful trajectories are inserted into the pool; there is no described dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or link-and-evolve of existing entries. The maximum pool size of 1000 implies an implicit capacity bound (some eviction/forgetting once full), but no explicit mutation/merging of stored trajectories is described.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case/trajectory selection is a fixed weighted top-k heuristic (Score = 1/3 s1 + 1/3 s2 + 1/3 s3 over an off-the-shelf embedder plus metadata signals). It is not an RL/value-optimized or learned retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or learned router). What evolves online is the pool CONTENT (via LLM-judged retain decisions), not the selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one SEER agent maintains and reads its own experience pool. No sharing of memory/experience across multiple agents or heterogeneous agent frameworks. (A GPT-4o user simulator participates in tau-bench but is the environment/user, not a memory-sharing agent.)
benchmarks: ToolQA (Zhuang et al. 2023): 8 real-world domains (air transportation/Flight, financial/Coffee, commercial services/Yelp, lodging/Airbnb, social networks/DBLP graph, academic publications/SciREX, personal agendas/Agenda, numerical reasoning/GSM8K); easy set = 800 questions / 55 templates, hard set = 730 questions / 62 templates. tau-bench (Yao et al. 2025): multi-turn tool-agent-user interaction in two real-world domains, airline (50 tasks, 13 tools) and retail (115 tasks, 15 tools), 165 tasks total, with a GPT-4o user simulator.
benchmark_family: tool (ToolQA, tau-bench). ToolQA is a multi-step tool-augmented QA benchmark spanning structured DBs, graph DB, and text corpora; tau-bench is a multi-turn tool-agent-user interaction benchmark. (Both are tool-use benchmarks; ToolQA also has a QA flavor.)
baselines: On ToolQA (foundation LLM Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for all): Chameleon (Lu et al. 2023), CoT, ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), TUMS (He et al. 2025), ART (Paranjape et al. 2023), and ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) [ExpeL is the strongest/second-best overall]; full table also lists Direct and CoT-noTool. On tau-bench, reference models: closed-source Claude 3.5 Sonnet (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022), GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-11-20), GPT-4o-mini (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18); open-source DeepSeek-V3-0324, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; SEER is compared against the base Qwen2.5-7B/72B (SEER-enhanced vs original).
key_metrics: ToolQA: Accuracy (%) per domain and average accuracy Acc^avg across domains (separate easy/hard averages). tau-bench: pass^k (probability an agent succeeds in all k independent dialogue trials); pass^1 reported by default (single-shot success rate / average reward across tasks). NOTE: in tau-bench, k denotes number of trials, whereas elsewhere in the paper k denotes number of demonstrations.
headline_result: On ToolQA, SEER (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) achieves the best average accuracy across all tasks, outperforming the second-best baseline ExpeL by +6.1% on easy (67.9 vs 61.8 avg) and +4.7% on hard (31.1 vs 26.4 avg). On tau-bench, integrating SEER yields gains of +7.44% for Qwen2.5-7B (9.34 -> 16.78 avg) and +23.38% for Qwen2.5-72B (28.46 -> 51.84 avg); SEER(72B) at 51.84% approaches GPT-4o at 54.76%.
ablations: (1) Retrieval-strategy ablation (Fig.3): removing any of the three scoring components degrades performance vs full SEER. SEER(w/o s3 intent-match) drops most on EASY questions (intent alignment helps straightforward tasks); SEER(w/o s2 toolchain-coverage) drops most on HARD questions (toolchain coverage is crucial for complex multi-tool dependencies); SEER(query-based) (using only first-query similarity instead of full-trajectory similarity) drops only modestly, since ToolQA is a one-turn multi-step setting where the query is fixed across turns. (2) Demonstration number / top-k (Table 5, k in {0,2,4,6,8}): accuracy rises then falls, peaking at k=4 (SEER easy avg 67.88%, hard avg 31.51%); query-based SEER peaks at k=4 easy / k=6 hard. (3) Self-improvement (Fig.2): on 1,530 ToolQA questions shuffled into 10 batches of 153, batch accuracy rises from 37.7% (batch 1) to surpassing baselines by batch 5 (52.3%) and reaching 54.9% by the last batch (3-point moving average smoothed). (4) SEER+Reflection (Table 6): raises ToolQA to 69.0% easy / 32.0% hard, recovering the Coffee-Easy drop caused by cumbersome exemplars.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics are reported (ToolQA accuracy, tau-bench pass^1). No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately; retrieval quality is assessed only indirectly via component-ablation effects on task accuracy.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final task accuracy / pass^1 success rate). The self-improvement experiment adds a process-over-time view (per-batch accuracy trajectory showing online learning), and ablations attribute outcome to specific scoring components, but there is no formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness, retrieval-precision, or trajectory-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Framed qualitatively as a training-free / annotation-light efficiency win: SEER requires NO additional model training (vs RL methods StepTool/SWiRL) and NO manually curated/pre-collected demonstration libraries (vs ART/ExpeL reliance), reducing offline expert effort. Efficiency-vs-accuracy is managed via the top-k sweep (best at k=4; too many demonstrations overwhelm the model and reduce accuracy) and a capped pool size (1000). No explicit token-count, latency, dollar-cost, or rollout-count figures are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-managed by demonstration count. Default top-k = 4 retrieved exemplars (ablated 0-8; performance peaks at k=4 and declines beyond, indicating an implicit context budget where excess demonstrations cause confusion). Initial demonstration pool: 8 examples for ToolQA, 2 for tau-bench; experience pool capped at 1000. Max interaction steps T = 6 (ToolQA) and T = 30 (tau-bench). Scoring weights lambda_1=lambda_2=lambda_3=1/3. Selection is fixed-k retrieved-then-used (no adaptive/precision-driven k).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks). For reference: ToolQA easy 800 questions / 55 templates, hard 730 / 62 templates across 8 domains (structured DBs, graph DB, text corpora); tau-bench airline 50 tasks / 13 tools, retail 115 tasks / 15 tools (165 total), multi-turn with a GPT-4o user simulator. The repo includes dataset-generation notebooks to regenerate ToolQA easy/hard variants.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (stepwise multi-dimensional recall of successful trajectories), Reuse: yes (trajectories injected verbatim as fewshot exemplars), Revise: no (retrieved cases are not adapted/edited; the optional Reflection add-on only self-corrects the agent's own reasoning, not the cases), Retain: yes (LLM-judge gated online write-back of successful trajectories to the experience pool)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as experience replay / self-guided in-context learning and self-improvement; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under an experience-recall / experience-replay framing (citing ExpeL and LLM-as-a-judge).
builds_on: ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024, experience-pool / experiential-learning problem formulation that SEER explicitly builds its formulation upon and is the strongest baseline); ART (Paranjape et al. 2023, retrieval of similar multi-step reasoning/tool traces); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023, think-act-observe tool-use loop); in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020); LLM-as-a-judge (Li et al. 2024, used as the success evaluator for write-back); bge-large-en-v1.5 / C-Pack embeddings (Xiao et al. 2024); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023, basis for the optional SEER+Reflection variant). Backbone LLMs: Qwen2.5-7B/72B-Instruct (Qwen et al. 2025).
contrasts_with: Coarse-grained / task-similarity-only retrieval methods (ART, ExpeL) that overlook tool-chain alignment - SEER adds fine-grained stepwise scoring (toolchain coverage + intent match); methods relying on manually curated or pre-collected task-specific demonstration libraries (Zhao et al. 2024; Xu et al. 2024) - SEER self-accumulates experiences online; RL-based tool-learning that needs additional training (StepTool, Yu et al. 2024; SWiRL, Goldie et al. 2025) - SEER is training-free experience replay; self-improvement methods using static offline datasets (ExpeL, Tian et al. 2024 MCTS) - SEER updates its pool online during deployment.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). An experience/case-based, training-free tool-use agent in the lineage ReAct -> ART/ExpeL -> SEER: it advances experience-replay tool-use by (i) fine-grained stepwise retrieval scoring trajectory similarity + toolchain coverage + intent alignment, and (ii) online (test-time) growth of a self-judged experience pool, distinguishing it from static/offline experiential-learning predecessors and from RL-trained tool-learning.
